sources.label: Issuer JLTXX launch and Ethereum identity

reserveReview.rationale: The single slice identifies the direct government-MMF shareholder claim, matching the live adapter's exact class4397 key, rather than fabricating Treasury/repo/cash percentages from NAV. The filed mandate limits Treasury purchases to remaining or original maturities of 93 days and permits fully collateralized overnight repos. The October 1 issuer statistics give WAM/WAL of 13 days and daily/weekly liquid assets of 99.99%; these are dated issuer figures, not independent whole-book assurance or measured unconditional redemption capacity.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Direct Token Class fund-share exposure, valued by the exact issuer class publisher; no position-level look-through allocation asserted
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The direct instrument is fully identified. Current underlying security weights, repo counterparties, subcustody allocation, encumbrance and an exact-fund independent reserve-to-liability report remain unverified; the single fund-share slice does not claim a complete look-through census.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: The slice represents this token's direct fund-share claim, not a distinct tracked upstream stablecoin or an additional reserve asset. NAV verifies valuation, not independent portfolio assurance.

sources.label: SEC-filed JLTXX SAI, Part II custody and fund accounting

custodyProfile.uncertainty: The SAI names JPMorgan Chase Bank as custodian and fund accountant holding portfolio securities/cash and books of account; it is affiliated with the adviser and administrator. This establishes its service role, not independent assurance, current provider shares, every material repo/subcustody layer, account segregation, rehypothecation or a complete insolvency waterfall. Aggregate custodyModel stays unknown rather than treating the named bank as complete custody coverage.
